subject: MSA + Order Form: derivative control & feedback-license — proposed compromise
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cloudwave.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on MSA redline: output ownership / training / feedback license

Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — team liked the throughput metrics. Legal and procurement ran a first pass on the MSA + Order Form and surfaced three sticking points related to productization:

1) Output ownership: procurement wants a clear assignment for model-generated outputs used to build CloudWave-branded products. They asked whether Redwood would agree to assignment (or a broad license) for outputs produced by CloudWave prompts.

2) Training / retraining: CloudWave needs assurance that Redwood will not train models on their prompts or customer data without an explicit opt-in; they prefer an explicit "no-training" clause unless they sign a separate training license.

3) Feedback / telemetry: they want to provide usage feedback to Redwood in a way that doesn’t grant us rights to reuse it for productization — essentially, a narrow telemetry license for service improvements only.

Can we loop in legal for concrete language? Procurement asked for our suggested compromise by Monday so they can circulate to their GC. I attached their redline (PDF) but will also upload via DocuSign later if that helps.

Would appreciate a quick call if that makes it easier.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Morales
Sr. Manager, Procurement — CloudWave
[Attachment: CloudWave_firstpass_redline.pdf (PDF, 95KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-23T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Questions on MSA redline: output ownership / training / feedback license

Laura / Priyom — forwarding CloudWave's note below. They've asked us for a compromise by Monday. High level ask: assignment of outputs for productization + strict no-training unless opted-in + narrow telemetry/feedback license.

Quick thoughts:
- We shouldn't assign underlying model IP or our weights; we can offer a broad perpetual, worldwide license to use outputs in their products.
- For training, we can promise a default "no-use-for-training" for customer prompts & content unless they opt in via a signed training license. We may want to include an exception for anonymized, aggregated telemetry used for service stability (but they asked to limit that).
- For feedback, propose a limited license: "non-exclusive, royalty-free, revocable for safety issues, used only for service improvement, not for productization or training of customer-facing models."

Can you take a pass on short paragraph language we can send back? If legal is comfortable, I can attach our redlined MSA + order form and offer a 30-minute call with their GC.

Thanks — Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-24T14:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Questions on MSA redline: output ownership / training / feedback license

On Fri, Aug 23, 2025 at 9:12 AM Elena Morales <elena.morales@cloudwave.com> wrote:
> Karthik,
>
> Thanks for the demo last week — team liked the throughput metrics. Legal and procurement ran a first pass on the MSA + Order Form and surfaced three sticking points related to productization:
>
> 1) Output ownership: procurement wants a clear assignment for model-generated outputs used to build CloudWave-branded products. They asked whether Redwood would agree to assignment (or a broad license) for outputs produced by CloudWave prompts.

Karthik / Priyom — quick legal read and proposed language below. Kept it concise so we can send to Elena without dragging in GC for another back-and-forth unless they push.

Summary of our position (recommended compromise):
- Output: Offer a perpetual, worldwide, transferable, non-exclusive license to Customer to use, reproduce, modify, and distribute Model Outputs for Customer's internal and productized use. We will not assign title to Redwood's underlying models, weights, or training code. This aligns with our standard approach and preserves core IP.

- Training / Retraining: Insert a clause: "Redwood shall not use Customer-provided prompts, uploaded content, or response logs to further train or adapt any Redwood models for commercial deployment unless Customer provides prior written consent via a separate training license agreement." Add narrow operational exception: non-identifying, aggregated telemetry may be used for service stability and bug fixes (not for model training or productization).

- Feedback / Telemetry: Provide a limited feedback license: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, royalty-free, revocable license to use Customer feedback and telemetry solely to improve Redwood's hosted services and not to create Customer-specific product offerings or to train Customer-facing models, except with Customer's prior written consent." Also add a right for Customer to request deletion/removal of telemetry related to privacy or safety incidents.

Next steps I recommend:
1) I will prepare a redline of the MSA + Order Form with the three bullets above and a short cover note describing the compromise.
2) Priyom, please confirm whether we want to offer a 12-month carveout for any new model variants (e.g., if they buy a dedicated instance and we release a new base model) or keep indefinite protective language.
3) Karthik, offer a 30-min sync with their GC but keep legal on the call for any live counteroffers.

I'm attaching the proposed redline and a 1-page summary you can send to the customer. I kept the language tight to reduce negotiation iterations.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_proposed_output_training_feedback_redline.pdf (PDF, 42KB)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@cloudwave.com>, procurement@cloudwave.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: 2025-08-25T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: MSA + Order Form: proposed compromise on outputs, training, and feedback

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Per our conversation and Laura's suggested language, attached are: 1) a redlined MSA that reflects the compromise (perpetual license to outputs; no training without opt-in; narrow telemetry exception) and 2) a redlined Order Form (v3) with a short note on how productization scope maps to order line items.

High-level bullets you can circulate to GC:
- Outputs: Redwood offers Customer a perpetual, worldwide, transferable, non-exclusive license to use Model Outputs in Customer products. This grants CloudWave rights to build, sell and sublicense downstream products containing those outputs without Redwood assigning model IP.
- Training: Redwood will not use Customer prompts, uploaded files, or non-anonymized response logs to train or adapt models for commercial deployment without a separate signed training license. Redwood may retain aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service stability and debugging only (not for training).
- Feedback: Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use feedback and telemetry solely to improve Redwood's services; Redwood will not use feedback to create Customer-specific commercial models or productize customer data without explicit consent. Customer may request deletion of telemetry in safety/privacy incidents.

If this sounds acceptable, suggest the following next steps:
1) CloudWave: confirm acceptance of the three bullets above or indicate any material exceptions (e.g., absolute assignment request).
2) If accepted, final redlines get executed via DocuSign — link included below.
3) Offer: 30-min call early next week with Laura on the line for GC-level clarifications.

Attachments: [CloudWave_MSA_redline.pdf (PDF, 168KB)], [CloudWave_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx (DOCX, 76KB)]

Best,
